For an instant the opposing ranks heaved and struggled; for an instant Hillton repelled the attack; then, like a shot, the St. Eustace left tackle hurtled through and, avoiding the interference, nailed the Hillton runner six yards back of the line.

arxiv-2203-12157.title: Refined applications of Kato’s Euler systems for modular forms Thanks: Competing interests: The author declares none.
arxiv-2203-12157.creator: Chan-Ho Kim
arxiv-2203-12157.description: Abstract . We discuss refined applications of Kato’s Euler systems for modular forms of higher weight at good primes (with more emphasis on the non-ordinary ones) beyond the one-sided divisibility of the main conjecture and the finiteness of Selmer groups.

arxiv-2402-01099.creator: Ciprian Demeter
arxiv-2402-01099.description: Abstract . We prove (essentially) sharp L 4 L^{4} level set estimates for the periodic Schrödinger maximal operator in a certain range of the cut-off parameter. 1. Introduction We use number theory and elementary graph theory to prove the following level set estimate. Theorem 1.1 . Assume \|a_{n}\|_{l^{2}}=1 and N^{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{10}}{\;\lessapprox}\;\lambda\leq N^{\frac{1}{2}} . Then |\{x\in[0,1]:\;\sup_{t}|\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_{n}e(nx+n^{2}t)|\geq\lambda\}|{\;\lessapprox}\;\frac{N}{\lambda^{4}}.

arxiv-2405-05368.title: The minimum orientable genus of the repeated Cartesian product of graphs
arxiv-2405-05368.creator: Marietta Galea, John Baptist Gauci
arxiv-2405-05368.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marietta Galea, John Baptist Gauci. Determining the minimum genus of a graph is a fundamental optimisation problem in the study of network design and implementation as it gives a measure of non-planarity of graphs. In this paper, we are concerned with determining the smallest value of g g such that a given graph G G has an embedding on the orientable surface of genus g g .

arxiv-2410-12461.title: Challenges, Methods, Data – a Survey of Machine Learning in Water Distribution Networks
arxiv-2410-12461.creator: Valerie Vaquet, Fabian Hinder, André Artelt
arxiv-2410-12461.description: Abstract Research on methods for planning and controlling water distribution networks gains increasing relevance as the availability of drinking water will decrease as a consequence of climate change. So far, the majority of approaches is based on hydraulics and engineering expertise. However, with the increasing availability of sensors, machine learning techniques constitute a promising tool.

arxiv-2512-09329.title: Self Distillation Fine-Tuning of Protein Language Models Improves Versatility in Protein Design
arxiv-2512-09329.creator: Amin Tavakoli, Raswanth Murugan, Ozan Gokdemir, Arvind Ramanathan, Frances Arnold, Anima Anandkumar
arxiv-2512-09329.description: Abstract Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is a standard approach for adapting large language models to specialized domains, yet its application to protein sequence modeling and protein language models (PLMs) remains ad hoc. This is in part because high-quality annotated data are far more difficult to obtain for proteins than for natural language.

pmc-10546631.title: Implementation of web-based respondent driven sampling in epidemiological studies
pmc-10546631.creator: Pedro Ferrer-Rosende, María Feijoo-Cid, María Isabel Fernández-Cano, Sergio Salas-Nicás, Valeria Stuardo-Ávila, Albert Navarro-Giné
pmc-10546631.description: BackgroundRespondent-driven sampling (RDS) is a peer chain-recruitment method for populations without a sampling frame or that are hard-to-reach. Although RDS is usually done face-to-face, the online version (WebRDS) has drawn a lot of attention as it has many potential benefits, despite this, to date there is no clear framework for its implementation.

pmc-10746974.title: Implementation of Remote Activity Sensing to Support a Rehabilitation Aftercare Program: Observational Mixed Methods Study With Patients and Health Care Professionals
pmc-10746974.creator: Ziyuan Lu, Tabea Signer, Ramona Sylvester, Roman Gonzenbach, Viktor von Wyl, Christina Haag
pmc-10746974.description: BackgroundPhysical activity is central to maintaining the quality of life for patients with complex chronic conditions and is thus at the core of neurorehabilitation. However, maintaining activity improvements in daily life is challenging. The novel Stay With It program aims to promote physical activity after neurorehabilitation by cultivating self-monitoring skills and habits.

pmc-11372239.title: Germline mutation rate predicts cancer mortality across 37 vertebrate species
pmc-11372239.creator: Stefania E Kapsetaki, Zachary T Compton, Walker Mellon, Orsolya Vincze, Mathieu Giraudeau, Tara M Harrison, Lisa M Abegglen, Amy M Boddy, Carlo C Maley, Joshua D Schiffman
pmc-11372239.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and objectivesCancer develops across nearly every species. However, cancer occurs at unexpected and widely different rates throughout the animal kingdom. The reason for this variation in cancer susceptibility remains an area of intense investigation.

pmc-11404172.title: Bridging gaps and seeding futures: A synthesis of soil salinization and the role of plant-soil interactions under climate change
pmc-11404172.creator: Hao Tang, Lei Du, Chengcheng Xia, Jian Luo
pmc-11404172.description: SummarySoil salinization, exacerbated by climate change, poses significant threats to agricultural productivity, land restoration, and ecosystem resilience. This study reviews current knowledge on plant-soil interactions as a strategy to mitigate soil salinization induced by climate change, focusing on their role in soil salinity dynamics and tolerance mechanisms.

pmc-11509244.title: Investigating the Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Various Brown Algae Species
pmc-11509244.creator: Selin Ersoydan, Thomas Rustemeyer, Ripoll Lionel
pmc-11509244.description: This literature review investigated the anti-inflammatory properties of brown algae, emphasizing their potential for dermatological applications. Due to the limitations and side effects associated with corticosteroids and immunomodulators, interest has been growing in harnessing therapeutic qualities from natural products as alternatives to traditional treatments for skin inflammation.

pmc-11530752.title: Are all ultra-processed foods bad for health?
pmc-11530752.creator: Carlos Augusto Monteiro, Leandro FM Rezende
pmc-11530752.description: eakfast cereals, at the expense of non-UPFs, reduces the risk of type 2 diabetes. According to them, “this questions the use of an overall UPF metric for public guidance and supports recommendations to focus efforts on reducing consumption of specific UPFs.” There are several concerns with this claim.

pmc-11609425.title: Characterization of Staphylococcus lugdunensis biofilms through ethyl methanesulfonate mutagenesis
pmc-11609425.creator: McKenna J Cruikshank, Justine M Pitzer, Kimia Ameri, Caleb V Rother, Kathryn Cooper, Austin S Nuxoll
pmc-11609425.description: Staphylococcus lugdunensis is a coagulase-negative species responsible for a multitude of infections. These infections often resemble those caused by the more pathogenic staphylococcal species, Staphylococcus aureus, such as skin and soft tissue infections, prosthetic joint infections, and infective endocarditis. Despite a high mortality rate and infections that differ from other coagulase-negative species, little is known regarding S. lugdunensis pathogenesis.

pmc-11652436.title: Socioeconomic and geographic variation in adjuvant chemotherapy among elderly patients with stage III colon cancer in Norway – a national register-based cohort study
pmc-11652436.creator: Elin Marthinussen Gustavsen, Stig Norderval, Liv Marit Dørum, Aina Balto, Ragnhild Heimdal, Barthold Vonen, Eva Stensland, Ellinor Haukland, Beate Hauglann
pmc-11652436.description: BackgroundAbout half of the patients diagnosed with colon cancer are 70 years or older. Standard treatment for stage III colon cancer is major surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT). Norwegian guidelines recommend initiation of ACT within 6 weeks after resection.

pmc-12595787.title: Ferroptosis-related genes MDM2 and CDKN1A as potential biomarkers for COPD
pmc-12595787.creator: Rui Shi, Lueli Wang, Chunyun Bai, Fang Wang, Chaozhong Li, Chuang Xiao, Alex F Chen, Weimin Yang
pmc-12595787.description: ObjectiveChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by inflammation and an immune response. However, the relationship between ferroptosis and COPD remains unknown. We aim to identify pivotal ferroptosis-related biomarkers in COPD and explore their roles in immune infiltration landscapes.MethodsDifferentially expressed genes (DEGs) were obtained from all current datasets of peripheral blood and lung tissues associated with COPD.

pmc-12662322.title: Development and validation of an explainable machine learning model for preoperative prediction of central lymph node metastasis in capsular-invasive papillary thyroid carcinoma
pmc-12662322.creator: Jingchao Chen, Yingting Hong, Haolin Shen, Hong Chen
pmc-12662322.description: This study aimed to develop an explainable machine learning framework integrating dual-modality ultrasonography and thyroid function parameters for preoperative prediction of central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in capsular-invasive papillary thyroid carcinoma. A retrospective cohort of 382 pathologically confirmed capsular-invasive papillary thyroid carcinoma patients was stratified into CLNM-negative and CLNM-positive cohorts.

pmc-12751569.title: Examining the role of social determinants of health in alcohol-exposed pregnancy risk among American Indian women
pmc-12751569.creator: Jessica D. Hanson, Carolyn Noonan, Makenzie Clough, Robert Rosenman, Kyra Oziel, Karen Little Wounded, Michelle Sarche, Dedra Buchwald
pmc-12751569.description: Context and purposeAlcohol-exposed pregnancy (AEP) is a public health issue that impacts women from all backgrounds and nationalities. In particular, little is known about American Indian women at risk for AEP during the preconceptual period. The purpose of this paper is to characterize the social determinants of health among American Indian women at risk for AEP in the Great Plains.

pmc-12813070.title: Factors affecting contraceptive use among women seeking induced abortion in Hubei, China: a multicenter cross-sectional study
pmc-12813070.creator: Yun Tao, Chun Feng, Youling Zeng, Yujuan Li, Xin Du, Ling Zhang, Dan Li, Wenhua Zhang, Jiawei Kang, Juan Liu, Yuan Lu, Xia Sun, Yuanzhen Zhang
pmc-12813070.description: BackgroundContraception plays a vital role in improving maternal and neonatal health by preventing unintended pregnancies. This study aimed to assess the history of contraceptive use and identify factors influencing contraceptive behavior among women seeking induced abortion in central China.MethodsA multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in 25 hospitals across Hubei province.

pmc-13216122.title: Ethylmalonic and Methylsuccinic Acids Disrupt Bioenergetics and Induce Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Through Thiol Redox Modulation in Rat Striatum: Potential Mechanisms Involved in Ethylmalonic Encephalopathy
pmc-13216122.creator: Manuela Bianchin Marcuzzo, Ângela Beatris Zemniaçak, Jaqueline Santana da Rosa, Bianca Silveira Signorini Verdi, Maria Paula Dalla Vechia Benati, Josyane de Andrade Silveira, Juliana Gomes do Nascimento, Helena de Almeida Moreira, Mateus Dias-Oliveira, Diogo Onofre Souza, Alexandre Umpierrez Amaral,
pmc-13216122.description: Ethylmalonic (EMA) and methylsuccinic (MSA) acids concentrations are elevated in tissues and body fluids of patients with ethylmalonic encephalopathy (EE), a mitochondrial disorder associated with basal ganglia abnormalities. To clarify the pathophysiology of this disorder, we evaluated the effects of EMA and MSA on bioenergetics, redox homeostasis and mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) in rat striatum.

pmc-13396727.title: Interaction between systemic arterial reservoir behavior and cerebrovascular vasoreactivity during acute controlled hypocapnia
pmc-13396727.creator: Yaren Alan, Ahmet Tas, Muhammed Ikbal Bayhan, Alp Ozcan, Irem Sezer, Türker Kundak, Sabahattin Umman, Tim P van de Hoef, Jan J Piek, Kim H Parker, Murat Sezer
pmc-13396727.description: Cerebral carbon dioxide (CO2) vasoreactivity (CVR), defined as the dilatory capacity of cerebral vessels in response to CO2, has pathophysiological importance and is clinically relevant. Reservoir–excess pressure analysis (REPA) of arterial blood pressure (ABP) waveforms, which estimates the pressure-buffering (reservoir) capacity of large arteries, provides contemporary insights beyond standard ABP measures by encompassing global arterial compliance and vascular tone.

pmc-13401007.title: Mediation of the association between physical activity and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in children and adolescents by inflammatory markers: an analysis of 2017‒2020 NHANES data
pmc-13401007.creator: Chunyang Zhang, Xiaonan Li
pmc-13401007.description: Highlights•It examined the mediating role of inflammatory markers in the association of PA with MAFLD risk in children and adolescents.•This study clarified the mediating role of inflammatory markers in the relation of PA to MAFLD risk.•This study may inform the development of evidence-based health promotion policies and tailored public health strategies.

pmc-13500230.title: Effects of an 8-week mental preparation program combining progressive muscle relaxation and mental imagery on self-determined motivation and dynamic postural control in youth female handball players: an experimental study
pmc-13500230.creator: Imen Saket, Chiraz Goumni, Achraf Hammami, Adel Driss, Raouf Hammami, Imen Ben Amar
pmc-13500230.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionMental preparation strategies are widely used in youth sport to enhance both psychological and motor performance; however, the combined effects of progressive muscle relaxation and mental imagery on self-determined motivation and dynamic postural control remain insufficiently explored. This study investigated the effects of an 8-week mental preparation program combining Jacobson’s progressive muscle relaxation and mental imagery in cadet female handball players.MethodsA quasi-experimental pretest-post-test design with two parallel groups was employed.
